S.FORM: tia=ku pu-a-iisua sua tia=pi=kia tanam r<um>a-riŋai miana.
S.PHON: tiaku puaiisua sua tiapikia tanam rumariŋai miana
S.FORM: tiaku puaiisua sua tiapikia tanam r<um>aringai miana.
S.PHON: tiaku puaiisua sua tiapikia tanam [r|ɾ]uma[r|ɾ]iŋai miana
S.TRANSL: I shall talk about how to try setting up traps in the past.

S.FORM: iiku miana ia, ni-m-ari-avici ʔikua sua na=kanaʔua=maku "tia=r<um>a-riŋai=kani," misai.
S.PHON: iiku miana ia nimariavitʂi ʔikua sua nakanaʔuamaku tiarumariŋaikani misai
S.FORM: iiku miana ia, nimariavici 'ikua sua nakana'uamaku "tiar<um>aringaikani," misai.
S.PHON: iiku miana ia nima[r|ɾ]iavitʂi ʔikua sua nakanaʔuamaku tia[r|ɾ]uma[r|ɾ]iŋaikani misai
S.TRANSL: My deceased older brother took me and said, "We'll set up traps."
He said he would teach me how to set up traps.
I was very happy at that time.

S.FORM: si sua ni-m-ari-avici ʔikua ia, naa=kanaʔua=maku "sumio" kisa-ən.
S.PHON: ʂi sua nimariavitʂi ʔikua ia naakanaʔuamaku sumio kisaən
S.FORM: si sua nimariavici 'ikua ia, naakana'uamaku "sumio" kisaen.
S.PHON: ʂi sua nima[r|ɾ]iavitʂi ʔikua ia naakanaʔuamaku sumio kisaen
S.TRANSL: Because the deceased brother who took me was called Sumio 澄男.
He said he was taking me to set up traps.
I was happy because there were still many muntjacs at that time.

S.FORM: taavalaʔə=ci=kia r<um>iŋai ia, tee=ci=kia m-ara-cii-cii-cini r<um>iŋai misa=ku.
S.PHON: taavaɾaʔətʂikia rumiŋai ia teetʂikia maratʂiitʂiitʂini rumiŋai misaku
S.FORM: taavara'ecikia r<um>ingai ia, teecikia maraciiciicini r<um>ingai misaku.
S.TRANSL: I knew about how to set up traps, and I thought I could set up traps by myself.
(My brother) took me to set up only one trap.

S.FORM: t<um>u-tuuturu ʔikua a-pa-cəʔəra-a, "maka-sia nu r<um>iŋai=kia," misai.
S.PHON: tumutuuturu ʔikua apaʦəʔəraa makaʂia nu rumiŋaikia misai
tumutuutu[r|ɾ]u ʔikua apaʦeʔe[r|ɾ]aa makaʂia nu [r|ɾ]umiŋaikia misai
S.TRANSL: He told me to look at him, "Do it like this as I set up a trap," he said.

FORM.notes: Source parenthetical expanded under POL-026/POL-027; exact source and decision are in source_notation_audit.csv.

S.TRANSL: I was sitting there so that I could see it well.

FORM.notes: Source parenthetical expanded under POL-026/POL-027; exact source and decision are in source_notation_audit.csv.

S.TRANSL: I was sitting there so that I could see it well.

S.PHON: makaʂian ava rumariŋai misaku nakai taramanmanəŋənnaku
S.TRANSL: I thought, "That was how to set up a trap." But I saw it well.
I thought, "Certainly I was able to do it like him."

S.FORM: maa-caŋ-caŋarə=ci=kia si tee=ci=kia taavalaʔə r<um>iŋai misa=ku.
S.PHON: maaʦaŋʦaŋarətʂikia ʂi teetʂikia taavaɾaʔə rumiŋai misaku
S.FORM: maacangcangarecikia si teecikia taavara'e r<um>ingai misaku.
S.TRANSL: I was happy because I thought I was able to set up a trap.

S.FORM: ma-kaasi ʔikua na=kanaʔua=maku, "nu ʔuuna=cu=kasu tee=sətəa-na ia, tanam-a mu-kusa ʔinia," misai.
S.PHON: makaaʂi ʔikua nakanaʔuamaku nu ʔuunaʦukasu teesətəana ia tanama mukusa ʔinia misai
S.FORM: makaasi 'ikua nakana'uamaku, "nu 'uunacukasu teeseteana ia, tanama mukusa 'inia," misai.
S.PHON: makaaʂi ʔikua nakanaʔuamaku nu ʔuunaʦukasu teeseteana ia tanama mukusa ʔinia misai
S.TRANSL: My late brother said this to me, "If you have enough time, try to go there (to set up traps).
"I've told you what would be a good (location) to set up a trap." (he) said.
"Yes," I said.

S.FORM: "tee=kia c<um>a-cəʔəra taniaara," kisa-ən=naku "tee=cu=ku mu-a-kusa ʔinia pas-ara-tanam," misa=ku.
S.PHON: teekia ʦumaʦəʔəra taniaara kisaənnaku teeʦuku muakusa ʔinia pasaratanam misaku
S.FORM: "teekia c<um>ace'era taniaara," kisaennaku "teecuku muakusa 'inia pasaratanam," misaku.
S.PHON: teekia ʦumaʦeʔe[r|ɾ]a taniaa[r|ɾ]a kisaennaku teeʦuku muakusa ʔinia pasa[r|ɾ]atanam misaku
S.TRANSL: "I'll see which day to go there and try it," I said.
Later I went (there) by myself.
At first, I would ask, "How shall I do it?"
(Then) I walked to Tanuuteecu far away.
"I set up traps and wondered how they would go," I thought.
I was hiding the snare I had made (to catch animals).
I stretched the rope.

S.FORM: sua talisi si-ari-avəŋə ia, ni-ari-vakan-an=ci ia, tee=cu ʔavunun ʔənai.
S.PHON: sua taɾiʂi ʂiariavəŋə ia niarivakanantʂi ia teeʦu ʔavunun ʔənai
S.FORM: sua tarisi siariavenge ia, niarivakananci ia, teecu 'avunun 'enai.
S.PHON: sua ta[r|ɾ]iʂi ʂia[r|ɾ]iaveŋe ia nia[r|ɾ]ivakanantʂi ia teeʦu ʔavunun ʔenai
S.TRANSL: The (wire) rope was stretched and hidden, covered with soil.
(I) inserted (four) wooden sticks (into the ground on both sides of the trap).

S.FORM: "kanə ni-a-ru-aim=ku mia-sua api-taarə nu kaa=kia a-pu-ʔi-ʔiarə," misa=ku.
S.PHON: kanə niaruaimku miasua apitaarə nu kaakia apuʔiʔiarə misaku
S.FORM: "kane niaruaimku miasua apitaare nu kaakia apu'i'iare," misaku.
S.PHON: kane nia[r|ɾ]uaimku miasua apitaa[r|ɾ]e nu kaakia apuʔiʔia[r|ɾ]e misaku
S.TRANSL: I thought, "I forgot then that a snare could be dangerous if I didn't work slowly (and carefully.)"

S.FORM: misai ʔikua ʔənai pasa-rupaŋ mari-nairi sua ʔənai.
S.PHON: misai ʔikua ʔənai pasarupaŋ marinairi sua ʔənai
misai ʔikua ʔenai pasa[r|ɾ]upaŋ ma[r|ɾ]inai[r|ɾ]i sua ʔenai
S.TRANSL: I covered the trap with soil well.

S.FORM: ma-naasə s<in>aaʔə=maku si sua vuunaŋa ia, ni-ara-akini=maku na paisi=maku.
S.PHON: manaasə ʂinaaʔəmaku ʂi sua vuunaŋa ia niaraakinimaku na paiʂimaku
S.FORM: manaase s<in>aa'emaku si sua vuunanga ia, niaraakinimaku na paisimaku.
S.PHON: manaase ʂinaaʔemaku ʂi sua vuunaŋa ia nia[r|ɾ]aakinimaku na paiʂimaku
S.TRANSL: I probably touched something (accidentally) because the spring pole hit between my thighs.
Or probably I touched the trap and soil (with my hands).
The trap caught (me right on the spot).
(The trap) hit my testicles between (the legs).
I lay there crying.

S.FORM: tia=vaa=kia ʔutu-iri-a nu r<um>iŋai=kia misa=ku mia-sua pa-cəpə-cəpəŋ.
S.PHON: tiavaakia ʔutuiria nu rumiŋaikia misaku miasua paʦəpəʦəpəŋ
S.FORM: tiavaakia 'utuiria nu r<um>ingaikia misaku miasua pacepecepeng.
S.PHON: tiavaakia ʔutui[r|ɾ]ia nu [r|ɾ]umiŋaikia misaku miasua paʦepeʦepeŋ
S.TRANSL: I then wondered if I had better stand to the side while setting up a trap.
Ever since I have come to know how to set up a trap.

S.FORM: tia=vaa=kia ʔutu-iri-a nu r<um>iŋai=kia, misa=kia pa-cəpə-cəpəŋ.
S.PHON: tiavaakia ʔutuiria nu rumiŋaikia misakia paʦəpəʦəpəŋ
S.TRANSL: I thought I should stand to the side while setting up a trap.
At that time, it was really…

S.FORM: nakai mari-niŋ-iri maamia ia, naa mari-vəcəkai-ni ma-livəlaʔə ʔaicuru.
S.PHON: nakai mariniŋiri maamia ia naa marivəʦəkaini maɾivəɾaʔə ʔaiʦuru
S.FORM: nakai mariningiri maamia ia, naa marivecekaini marivera'e 'aicuru.
S.PHON: nakai ma[r|ɾ]iniŋi[r|ɾ]i maamia ia naa ma[r|ɾ]iveʦekaini ma[r|ɾ]ive[r|ɾ]aʔe ʔaiʦu[r|ɾ]u
S.TRANSL: It hurt a lot just to hit the side, not to mention to hit the testicles in the center.

S.FORM: mia-sua ia, ma-naasə=pi=kia=ʔai taavalaʔə na pu-aiʔi taanaasa.
S.PHON: miasua ia manaasəpikiaʔai taavaɾaʔə na puaiʔi taanaasa
S.FORM: miasua ia, manaasepikia'ai taavara'e na puai'i taanaasa.
S.PHON: miasua ia manaasepikiaʔai taava[r|ɾ]aʔe na puaiʔi taanaasa
S.TRANSL: Then I might have the difficulty to return home.
The (stick) hit off the center of my testicles.
I could see that it became dark.

S.FORM: kanə cu-culu api-taarə iimu kisa-i ma-maaraŋ.
S.PHON: kanə ʦuʦuɾu apitaarə iimu kisai mamaaraŋ
S.FORM: kane cucuru apitaare iimu kisai mamaarang.
S.PHON: kane ʦuʦu[r|ɾ]u apitaa[r|ɾ]e iimu kisai mamaa[r|ɾ]aŋ
S.TRANSL: It's really dangerous, as the elders said.

S.FORM: nu ʔuuna=kamu kaa-manəŋ-a rəŋai ia, ka-sakən-au sua ʔaicuru=mu.
S.PHON: nu ʔuunakamu kaamanəŋa rəŋai ia kasakənau sua ʔaiʦurumu
S.FORM: nu 'uunakamu kaamanenga rengai ia, kasakenau sua 'aicurumu.
S.PHON: nu ʔuunakamu kaamaneŋa [r|ɾ]eŋai ia kasakenau sua ʔaiʦu[r|ɾ]umu
S.TRANSL: When you make a trap, watch out for your testicles.
In fact, it's really dangerous.
I'm telling here by the tape recorder.

S.FORM: ma-naasə tee=pa timana-ən siŋsi=maku ʔaisi taka-cii-cin-in=kiai mari-sunatə.
S.PHON: manaasə teepa timanaən ʂiŋʂimaku ʔaiʂi takatʂiitʂininkiai marisunatə
S.FORM: manaase teepa timanaen singsimaku 'aisi takaciicininkiai marisunate.
S.PHON: manaase teepa timanaen ʂiŋʂimaku ʔaiʂi takatʂiitʂininkiai ma[r|ɾ]isunate
S.TRANSL: The professor is still listening and writing by himself.
That's all I want to tell you.
